newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks fall steeply on Wall St drop.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks fall steeply on Wall St drop.

text.p: European stocks fell steeply on Tuesday, disheartened by a big drop on Wall Street as American investors took profits after last week's record-breaking run.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar, still buoyed by expectations over a soft single European currency, gained on the mark but was unchanged against the yen.

European bourses, already trading at a loss, were badly hit by Wall Street's negative start. London and Paris plunged by nearly 1.5 percent and Frankfurt's IBIS index of electronic trade was down one percent.

New York's early losses were despite a batch of U.S. economic figures which showed subdued inflationary pressures. Investors took the opportunity to pocket some of the gains from last week's big advance which set six closing records.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 0.5 percent within minutes of the U.S. data showing that consumer inflation and housing starts for May came in lower than expected.

London, which itself set a cracking pace last week with three closing records, suffered the most from Wall Street. The market already had enough worries about possible bad news in the British budget next month.

The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was down 76 points at 4,669.1 at one stage and investors were expected to remain in a selling mood after reports that the government could cut valuable tax breaks for pension funds in the July 2 budget.
"We are going to have budget blues," a trader said. "There's just no reason to buy this market."

"We're only three weeks away from the budget now and I think the market will continue to be nervous," said one trader. "We still look vulnerable to more profit-taking because there's a lot of profits to be taken."

In Paris, which saw volatile trading on Monday, the CAC 40 fell 50.04 points to 2,745.83 after strong advances last week. "We're seeing profit-taking on recent gains as the market waits for the new government's policy address" on Thursday, a broker said.
Frankfurt floor trade, which ended before Wall Street opened, finished down 0.63 percent.
But after-hours trading on the IBIS index fell further after New York's drop and an outbreak of jitters about the effectiveness of the single currency stability pact agreed at the Amsterdam summit.
"There is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," said one trader.
In currencies, the dollar shrugged off the U.S. data which kept prospects of higher interest rates at bay and held gains of half a pfennig against the mark.
The German currency remains under pressure and the dollar is benefiting from its safe haven reputation as the stability pact improved prospects for a weak single currency.

"Overall people do think EMU will progress and that the chances are it will be a weak one -- that's a reason the dollar's fairly well underpinned," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank in London.

The U.S. currency was largely unchanged on the yen with traders focusing on this week's Japanese May trade data, expected to show a growing surplus, and U.S. April figures, where a worsening deficit, is expected.

Anticipation of the data has added spice to speculation before leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations meet in Denver on June 20-22. The market fears that the expanding trade gap will see sparks fly between the United States and Japan. A stronger dollar helps Japanese exports.
Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered, said the United States was concerned about trade but not to the point that it was willing to engage heavily in exchange rate rhetoric.
"The issue is to try to get Japan to boost demand and how they do that, rather than by trying to engineer a manipulation of exchange rates," said Fox.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7337 marks and 113.40 yen, compared with 1.7291 and 113.39 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 63.3 points at 4,681.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 33.27 points at 2,762.60.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 23.63 points at 3,741.48.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.15 an ounce, compared with Monday's close of $341.75. Silver was unchanged at $4.79, up seven cents.
